newsitem.title: USA: Muni yield curve steepens over past week - Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Muni yield curve steepens over past week - Delphis.

text.p: The municipal yield curve steepened about five basis points in the week ended Thursday, as overall yields rose between five and 10 basis points, Delphis Hanover Corp said Friday.
The triple-A yield curve between one-year and 30-year bonds steepened five to 200 basis points. The Baa curve reversed the prior week's move, steepening five to 195 basis points.
The yield increases added to gains from an eroding market the prior week as well, Delphis said.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated municipal yields rose 10 basis points to 5.70 percent, while thirty-year Baa yields rose the same amount to 6.50 percent.
The yield increases closely matched gains in the Treasury market, where the government long bond rose eight basis points for the second week in a row to finish Thursday at 6.96 percent.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis were yielding 81.9 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday, compared to 81.4 percent the week before.
Average yields on one-year municipal bonds rose five basis points across the credit spectrum, rising to 3.70 percent in the Aaa category and 4.55 percent for Baa's.
Yields also rose five basis points in the intermediate sector, moving ten-year Aaa-rated bonds to 4.95 percent and Baa-rated ten-years to 5.80 percent.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was unchanged at 85 basis points, and the 30-year spread was also steady at 80 basis points.
